suggested_questions: He started pulling away right after we talked about moving in together — did I push too fast?
She shuts down mid-argument and acts totally normal the next day. Do I bring it back up?
He gives me little random gifts and insists they mean nothing. Am I reading too much into it?
We act like a couple but he won't call it one. How long should I wait for a label?

She said she never loved me the day she left. How much of that should I believe?
He came back after four months but nothing about him seems different. Do I let him in?

topics.label: Pulling away
topics.description: Why avoidants withdraw exactly when things get close — often right at a milestone — and how to give space without chasing or blaming yourself.

topics.label: Fights & shutdown
topics.description: What to do when they stonewall mid-conflict: space during the flood, words after it, and why next-day normalcy isn't indifference.

topics.label: Signs of love
topics.description: The easy-to-miss ways avoidants show attachment — acts of service, small gifts they immediately downplay, and things they've told no one else.

topics.label: Mixed signals & tests
topics.description: Decoding hot-and-cold behavior and deliberate "no"s — and where subconscious vetting crosses into a gauntlet you shouldn't try to endure.

topics.label: Am I a placeholder?
topics.description: The concrete contrasts that separate real avoidant love from a convenience dynamic, including consistent time together that never becomes closeness.

topics.label: Getting commitment
topics.description: Making each step feel safe: specific reassurance, honest pacing, and spacing out the milestones that tend to set off the exit.

topics.label: Boundaries & self-respect
topics.description: Saying what you need plainly, without ultimatums or self-abandonment — the one variable on your side that changes the dynamic most.

topics.label: When to walk away
topics.description: The red flags that mean this isn't an attachment problem to repair, and how to leave without anger or waiting it out for years.

topics.label: After the breakup
topics.description: How avoidants actually grieve — the early relief that isn't indifference, the delayed crash, and why a fast rebound proves nothing.

topics.label: The no contact rule
topics.description: What the silence is actually for, how long it usually runs, and what tends to happen on their side week by week.

topics.label: Blocked or ghosted
topics.description: How to read being blocked, ghosted, or slowly faded out — and what a lasting block honestly tells you about the door.

topics.label: Coming back or gone?
topics.description: The signals that a breakup isn't permanent, the ones that say it is, and how to decide whether you even want them back.

scenarios.title: They pulled away
scenarios.subtitle: Texts slowed down, plans stopped, and you don't know why
scenarios.question: My partner has been pulling away — fewer texts, no plans, more distance — and it started not long after we took a step forward together. What's actually happening on their side, how much space should I give before I say anything, and what should I avoid doing right now?

scenarios.title: They came back
scenarios.subtitle: After the silence they reached out — and you're unsure what to do
scenarios.question: My avoidant ex reached out after months of silence and wants to talk, but hasn't really explained anything. How do I tell whether anything has actually changed, how slowly should I move, and what shouldn't I bring up yet — so we don't just restart the same on-and-off cycle?

scenarios.title: Mixed signals
scenarios.subtitle: Warm one week, distant the next — decode what it means
scenarios.question: I'm getting mixed signals — warm and close one week, cold and distant the next, and lately they seem to be testing me in small ways. How do I tell whether this is avoidant deactivation, subconscious vetting, or genuine disinterest — and when does it stop being worth decoding?

scenarios.title: Making it work
scenarios.subtitle: You're staying — build safety, boundaries, and a real bond
scenarios.question: I want to make this work long term. How do I build enough safety that my avoidant partner stays connected — pacing the big milestones, giving space without disappearing, and asking for what I need — without losing myself or waiting forever for things to change?
